Where they meet in the bottom-right corner, Chrome painted a bright **white square** (the circled area) — glaringly out of place against the dark themed track and UI.\n\nThat corner is the `::-webkit-scrollbar-corner` pseudo-element. Chrome renders it as an opaque white box by default, and the stylesheet styled the scrollbar track and thumb but never the corner — so whenever both scrollbars appear together, the white default showed through.\n\n## The fix\n\nAdded a `::-webkit-scrollbar-corner` rule (in `public/stylesheets/styles.css`, next to the existing global scrollbar styles) setting its background to `transparent`, matching the already-transparent track. The corner now blends into the surrounding UI instead of showing a white block.\n\n```css\n::-webkit-scrollbar-corner {\n  background: transparent;\n}\n```\n\nThis is a global rule, so it fixes the corner everywhere both scrollbars co-occur, not just the Automator pane. The problem is visible on load with no interaction, consistent with the report, since it's purely a static styling gap."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":539,"cache_read_input_tokens":31004,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":539,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"00f7fafa-7232-4e2a-93cb-4274699b44be","uuid":"7b216b66-a90d-43c5-ba6c-f6baf4b497a3","timestamp":"2026-07-31T18:23:07.332Z"}
